channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold tumbles to eight-month low below $4,000 as Middle East tensions reinforce US rate hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) falls to near an eight-month low around $3,975 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal extends its downside as rising tensions in the Middle East raise inflation concerns and reinforce expectations of elevated US interest rates.

item.title: Fed’s Jefferson: Current policy is well positioned to respond, based on incoming data
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said that the current policy stance should support the job market and allow inflation to resume decline toward 2% as tariff effects and energy prices pass through, Reuters reported on Thursday.

item.title: South Korean Won: BoK hike and semiconductor volatility – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights a hawkish 25bp hike by the Bank of Korea (BoK) to 2.75%, with guidance that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and core inflation will exceed earlier forecasts.

item.title: The Japanese Yen is boxed between a floor it hates and a ceiling nobody trusts
item.description: Dollar-Yen has spent the week doing almost nothing at the most dramatic level in four decades.

item.title: Crude Oil watches the region catch fire and still cannot clear its ceiling
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude Oil is fading about one percent to just below $79.00 after a third consecutive failure at the $80.00 handle, where the 50-day Exponential Moving Average sits just above the figure and refuses to yield.

item.title: The Australian Dollar stalls exactly where everybody said it would
item.description: The Australian Dollar is going nowhere with great precision, with AUD/USD flat on the session and pinned to the 0.7000 handle for a fourth consecutive day.

item.title: The British Pound Sterling gets a new Prime Minister and an old problem
item.description: Sterling is enduring its heaviest session of the month, with GBP/USD fading around half of one percent to just below 1.3500 after the week's advance stalled short of 1.3550 for a second consecutive day.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Retreats from 18-year high, struggles at 220
item.description: The GBP/JPY retreats some 0.34% on Thursday after the pair reached a new 18-year high of 219.62 on Wednesday. Nevertheless, at the time of writing, the cross-pair retreated to 218.80, down 0.34%, as the Yen recovers some ground.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Upside bias toward 6.7600 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that USD/CNH downside momentum continues to build after the pair slipped to 6.7653. Intraday, there is a chance of testing major support at 6.7600 while staying below 6.7780.

item.title: South Korean Won: Hawkish BoK and equity correction support – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the Korean Won (KRW) is outperforming, supported by a hawkish 25 bps Bank of Korea (BoK) hike to 2.75% and expectations that growth and core inflation will exceed 2026 projections.

item.title: Thai Baht: Overvaluation points to weakness against US Dollar - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that softer US inflation data has weakened the Dollar and lowered Fed rate hike expectations, but USD/THB has still broken above 33.50.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Swissie rebounds at 0.8042 support
item.description: The USD/CHF reversed course, rising by over 0.40% late Thursday as the Greenback staged a recovery amid overall risk aversion, heightened tensions in the Middle East, and strong US economic data. The pair trades at 0.8088 after bouncing off daily lows of 0.8045.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar rises on resilient labor data, while Oil and Gold fall
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) rises toward 100.80, gaining around 0.3% as stronger-than-expected United States labor-market data supports the Greenback. US Initial Jobless Claims fell to 208K, below expectations of 217K and the previous 216K.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Further upside risk builds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD downside momentum has intensified after a sharp intraday swing, with firm support highlighted at 1.2875 and 1.2860.

item.title: Mexican Peso drops as risk aversion underpins the US Dollar
item.description: The Mexican Peso depreciated by about 0.30% on Thursday as market participants turned risk-averse amid an escalation of the Middle East conflict, which has driven energy prices higher.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual gains with capped upside against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that USD/CNY has extended its decline on softer United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI), with firmer People's Bank of China (PBoC) fixings validating gradual RMB appreciation.

item.title: Euro falls as strong US jobless claims support US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD trades lower near the 1.1440 area on Thursday, retreating around 0.2% as the US Dollar (USD) gains support from stronger-than-expected United States (US) labor market data.

item.title: European Union: Trade tools and China rebalancing – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered analysts Christopher Graham and Carol Liao discuss how the European Union is seeking to rebalance its trade relationship with China without shutting the door on engagement.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD tests the $55 floor as sellers retain control
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds and US Treasury yields stabilize following a two-day drop driven by softer-than-expected US inflation data. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $55.75, down 3.50% on the day.

item.title: Gold loses track of $4,000, drops as Oil shock revives Fed bets
item.description: Gold price drops over 1.80% as tensions between the US and Iran fuel fears of a possible Oil supply disruption, driving energy prices higher and potentially triggering another round of inflation. The XAU/USD trades at $3,994.

item.title: British Pound: Dips against US Dollar seen as buying opportunity – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note GBP/USD is slightly weaker as it gives back part of yesterday’s strong advance, helped by expectations of a centrist, market-friendly Burnham government.

item.title: Euro edges lower against the Japanese Yen despite ECB rate hike expectations
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 185.80 at the time of writing on Thursday, little changed on the day after reaching a one-month high earlier this week.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average discovers the virtue of owning few semiconductors
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) added roughly 160 points, or 0.3%, to trade near 52,800 on Thursday while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2% and the NASDAQ Composite shed 0.9%.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Buyers retain upper hand near one-month highs
item.description: NZD/USD fluctuates between minor gains and losses on Thursday as the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s (RBNZ) hawkish stance supports the Kiwi, while a stronger US Dollar (USD) caps the upside. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.5842 after climbing to a one-month high earlier this week.

item.title: British Pound pulls back as solid US data revives the Greenback
item.description: The Pound Sterling trims some of its Wednesday gains versus the US Dollar, down by over 0.48% following solid US data. The sell-off comes amid risk aversion and augments the safe-haven appeal of the Greenback. At the time of writing, the GBP/USD trades at 1.3375, after peaking near 1.3545.

item.title: Crude Oil watches the Houthis aim at the last export route that still works
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil spent Thursday's European morning grinding down to 78.37 before ripping nearly two dollars to 80.29 when the Houthis threatened to target all Saudi Oil sites and key facilities should Saudi Arabia escalate its actions against Yemen.

item.title: Gold tests $4,000 as energy-driven inflation fears keep Fed rate hike bets in play
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Thursday as traders look past back-to-back, softer-than-expected US inflation reports and remain focused on renewed Middle East tensions, which are fueling concerns that higher energy prices could reignite inflationary pressure.

item.title: Swiss Franc falls as Middle East tensions keep Fed rate hike expectations alive
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday as the Greenback regains its footing following a two-day decline. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.8080, up nearly 0.35% on the day, rebounding from an intraday low of 0.8044.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds above 0.7000 as US Retail Sales lose momentum
item.description: AUD/USD trades slightly higher near the 0.7010 area on Thursday, extending its recent recovery as the US Dollar (USD) struggles to gain sustained momentum following mixed United States (US) economic data.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Gains eye 1.3981 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/CAD is flat after the Bank of Canada (BoC) left policy unchanged and maintained a cautious tone on growth and inflation.
